title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a case of mistaken identification acted on as though it were confirmed. Deputies treated a car as a stolen Camaro linked to multiple aggravated robberies and moved on it with at least five patrol cars, a helicopter, drawn guns and handcuffs. The failure was in acting on the identification before verifying it, and the deputies could not read the plates at the scene.

Catching it required a verification step between the match and the stop. Running the plates, or reading them, would have shown the car was not the one being sought. The gap sits at the handoff between whatever identified the vehicle and the officers who surrounded two men who had just returned from a gas station.

What is not established: whether any automated plate-reading or database system produced the match, whether procedures were followed, and whether the deputy's threat was made as described. The sheriff's office review is pending, the account of the threat comes from the victims, and no finding of wrongdoing has been made.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in Cypress, Harris County sheriff's deputies mistook two 19 year old men, Anthony and Julian, for car thieves. The men had just returned from a gas station, and Anthony was about to leave in his Camaro when at least five patrol cars and a helicopter surrounded them. Deputies drew guns, handcuffed them, and a deputy threatened to shoot and kill Julian, who later had cuts and scrapes. Deputies thought the car was a stolen Camaro linked to multiple aggravated robberies, but they could not read the plates and later realized it was the wrong car.

Deputies explained they were looking for a stolen car. Anthony's mother, Leslie, wants deputies held accountable and plans to hire an attorney. She believes they could have run the plates or used a different approach. The Harris County Sheriff's Office said supervisors, including the district captain, shift lieutenants, and shift sergeants, will review body worn camera footage to check whether procedures were followed. The men were given information on filing a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
